questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct is regarding measures of money supply?

I. M1 and M2 are known as narrow money.

II. M3 and M4 are known as broad money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct statements regarding measures of money supply are that M1 and M2 are known as narrow money, and M3 and M4 are known as broad money: 
 
• **M1**
 
 
• Also known as narrow money, M1 is the most liquid form of money and is made up of currency in circulation and demand deposits in banks.
 
 
 
• **M2**
 
 
• A broader concept of money supply, M2 includes M1 plus savings deposits with post office savings banks.
 
 
 
• **M3**
 
 
• Also known as broad money or aggregate monetary resource, M3 includes M1 plus time deposits with the bank.
 
 
 
• **M4**
 
 
• Includes all items of M3 plus total deposits of post office saving accounts.
 
 
 
• These measures are in decreasing order of liquidity, with M1 being the most liquid and M4 being the least liquid. 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India publishes figures for these four alternative measures of money supply

questions.question: From which state, 'Pongal' festival belongs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Pongal festival is from Tamil Nadu. It is a four-day harvest festival celebrated in the state of Tamil Nadu, South India: 
 
• Pongal is celebrated in the month of Thai, which is January or February in the Gregorian calendar. 
 
• Pongal is a thanksgiving for a bountiful harvest and marks the end of the winter solstice and the start of spring.
 
• It is dedicated to the Sun God, Surya. 
 
• The festival is celebrated with the preparation of a sweet rice dish called Pongal, which is cooked with milk, jaggery, and cardamom.
 
• Other celebrations include bull-taming contests, a bonfire made of agricultural waste, and prayers for the family's prosperity. 
 
• The four days of Pongal are named Bhogi, Surya, Mattu, and Kaanum. 
 
• The name Pongal comes from the Tamil word Ponga, which means "to boil".

questions.question: Which of the following dance form is wedded with Hindustani music school?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Kathak is the classical dance form that is associated with Hindustani music: 
 
• Kathak is the only classical dance form that is associated with Hindustani or North Indian music.
 
• It is often performed with the accompaniment of tabla, sitar, and sarangi. 
 
• Kathak originated in Uttar Pradesh, North India. It has roots in the Mughal era. 
 
• Kathak is usually performed as a solo, with the dancer narrating stories from ancient scriptures through rhythmic footwork, hand gestures, facial expressions, and eye work. 
 
• Schools
 
• There are three main schools of Kathak, or Gharanas, which are the Jaipur Gharana, the Benaras Gharana, and the Lucknow Gharana.
 
• These schools differ in their emphasis on footwork versus acting. 
 
• Costumes
 
• Hindu female dancers wear a long pleated kurta over pajamas or a sari with traditional jewelry.

• The Veda Samaj was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj.

• They condemned the superstitions and rituals of orthodox Hinduism.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with Official language?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part XVII**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part XVII of the Indian Constitution deals with the Official Language**.
 
• It** includes Articles 343 to 351, **which outline provisions for the language to be used in the Union, States, and communication between them.
 
• It **also covers the promotion and development of the Hindi language** and the use of English alongside Hindi for official purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part XIX**:

 
 
• This part **deals with Miscellaneous Provisions of the Constitution.**
 
• It includes **Articles 361 to 367**, which cover topics such as the protection of the President
 
• It Governors from legal proceedings and the interpretation of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Part XVIII:**
 
 
• This part **deals with Emergency Provisions.**
 
• It includes **Articles 352 to 360, **which outline the types of emergencies in India: National Emergency, State Emergency (President’s Rule), and Financial Emergency.
 
• It** also describes the powers and procedures during these emergencie**s.
 
 
 
• **Part XVI:**
 
 
• This part is dedicated to **Special Provisions Relating to Certain Classes.**
 
• It includes** Articles 330 to 342,** which focus on the representation of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and other disadvantaged groups in Parliament and State Assemblies, as well as special provisions for the Anglo-Indian community.
